conventions: Body maps: north is at the top and east longitude increases to the right. centerLongitudeDeg is the east longitude at the image centre (null = unknown or not meaningful). For a point at east longitude L and latitude B: u = 0.5 + (L - centerLongitudeDeg) / 360 (modulo 1, from the left edge), v = (90 - B) / 180 (from the top edge). Where a longitude note says 'found by inspection' or 'check by inspection', the check is good to a few degrees only. Star map: right ascension 0 h is at the image centre and right ascension increases to the left; declination +90 degrees is at the top. For right ascension A and declination D in degrees: u = 0.5 - A / 360 (modulo 1, from the left edge), v = (90 - D) / 180 (from the top edge). Ring strip: see the note of the entry saturn_ring.

textures.title: Saturn Ring
textures.longitudeNote: not stated at the source
textures.note: PNG with transparency (straight alpha, not premultiplied). The horizontal axis is the distance from the centre of Saturn. The inner edge is at the left and the outer edge is at the right. The source does not state the inner and outer radius. Estimate (not from the source): a fit of the outer edge of the B ring and the outer edge of the A ring to the NASA Saturnian Rings Fact Sheet (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/satringfact.html) gives a linear scale of about 35.0 km per pixel of the 2048 pixel strip. The left edge of the image is then at about 69,300 km and the right edge is at about 141,050 km from the centre of Saturn (1.150 and 2.340 equatorial radii of 60,268 km). With this scale the inner edge of the C ring, the inner edge of the B ring, the Encke gap and the Keeler gap agree with the fact sheet to about 120 km. The F ring lies about 540 km outside of its fact sheet radius. Landmarks as fractions of the width: inner edge of the C ring 0.073, inner edge of the B ring 0.316, outer edge of the B ring 0.672, Encke gap 0.896, Keeler gap 0.936, outer edge of the A ring 0.941, F ring 0.990. The small file has 1024 x 63 pixels.
